name: AFMX residual risk index
note: Written and committed before the index was computed for the first time and before any comparison with market prices. This file is not edited afterwards. A different formula is version 2 in a new file, and both are shown.
what_the_author_had_seen: The 12 open cards and their forecast probabilities (they are the inputs). Not seen: the index value, its history, or any relation between it and any market price.
what_it_is: One number for how much unresolved event risk is on AFMX's open cards. It adds up AFMX's own judgment. It is a summary of opinions that are scored in public, not a measurement of the market and not a forecast of prices.

per_card_stage.resolved_or_withdrawn: 0, and the card leaves the sum
per_card_stage.open_or_easing_with_a_forecast: 1 - p_resolved + p_worsened, from the newest forecast written on or before the day. This is the expected stage at that forecast's deadline when resolved counts 0, still open 1 and worsened 2. Kept between 0 and 2.
per_card_stage.after_a_deadline_passes: The last forecast keeps counting until a new one is written.

formula.per_card_reach: 1 if aids/reading.json marks the card market_wide; otherwise the number of sectors it names as direct, divided by 11; never less than 1/11. Reach says how much of the US market a card touches. It is a count of sectors, not a measured size of damage.
formula.index: The sum over open cards of reach times stage. Unit: 'market-wide open risks'. A value of 5 reads as: the same as five risks that each touch the whole market and are expected to stay open.
published_with_it: the same sum with every reach set to 1 (a check on how much the reach weights matter)
each card's share of the index
tilt: the sum of reach times (p_worsened - p_resolved); above zero means the cards lean toward getting worse
formula.no_scale: The index is not rescaled to 0 to 100 and has no bands such as low or high. There is no history to set bands from. Bands may be proposed as version 2 after the first review.

history.how: Recomputed from the card files for every day on which a card was opened, changed status or got a new forecast. The day's status is the last status in the card's history on or before that day.
history.starts: 2026-11-26, the day the first cards were recorded. Nothing is back-filled before that.
history.reach_over_time: The reach in today's aids/reading.json is used for every day. If a card's reach is changed, the history shifts; such a change is recorded in residual/README.md with its date.

market_test.status: Not run. Until it is run and passed, AFMX makes no claim that this index says anything about prices.
market_test.earliest: 2027-11-26, and only with at least 52 weekly values and at least 10 weeks in each group below.
market_test.question: After the index rose over four weeks, was the AFMX market backdrop score (rule v3, 0 to 100, from records/) higher four weeks later than after the index fell or stayed the same?
market_test.method: Friday values. Group A: weeks where the index is higher than four weeks earlier. Group B: all other weeks. Outcome: backdrop score four weeks later minus the score that Friday. Statistic: mean of A minus mean of B, with a 90% range from a block bootstrap in blocks of four weeks.
market_test.passes_if: The whole 90% range is above zero.
market_test.if_it_fails_or_cannot_be_run: The page says so in plain words, and the index stays labeled as a summary of open cards only.
market_test.one_look: The test is run once on the date above. Looking earlier, or trying other outcomes, is reported as exploratory and cannot pass.

known_limits: Every input is AFMX's own judgment. The index moves only when AFMX edits a card, so it can lag events by up to a day and can be moved by AFMX's own mistakes.
12 cards. One card with wide reach can move the index by a fifth.
The number of cards is an editorial choice (selection/criteria.json). Opening more cards raises the index even if the world did not change.
Forecast deadlines differ from 2026-12-12 to 2027-06-30, so the stages are not over the same horizon.
Cards share causes (rates, AI spending). Adding them up counts shared causes more than once.
Reach is a count of sectors. A card that touches one sector can still do more damage than a market-wide one.
Two days of history on the day this was written.
